title: Integrate Hunch engineering memory system with IDE hooks for decision tracking
context: Engineering decisions, constraints, and bug root causes are often lost over time, leading to recurring bugs and drift between code intent and implementation. Manual documentation is unreliable and not queryable.
decision: Adopt Hunch as a persistent decision graph, integrated via MCP servers and IDE hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit). Provide CLI commands for capturing decisions, healing doc/code drift, analyzing fragility, and grounding bug fixes in past context.
consequences: All IDE sessions automatically invoke Hunch hooks for decision capture and query
Decisions persist in a queryable graph, preventing drift and informing future work
Bug fixes can reference past root causes and constraints via Hunch commands
Code understanding is grounded in documented rationale rather than inference
Fragility analysis and dependency discovery become queryable from the graph
Adds runtime overhead from hook invocations on every tool use and session start
alternatives_rejected: Markdown/wiki-based decision documentation (prone to drift, not queryable, separated from code)
Manual record-keeping in code comments (unreliable, not structured, easily lost)
No persistent memory system (decisions forgotten, root causes rediscovered, bugs recur)
